content.value_statement: Teams need a reliable way to observe new Gmail activity without manually refreshing inboxes. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code run gws Gmail watch workflows with filters and output controls.
actual_capabilities: Starts Gmail watch sessions with the gws gmail +watch command.
Streams new Gmail messages as newline-delimited event output.
Filters watched messages by Gmail label IDs such as INBOX or UNREAD.
Uses existing Pub/Sub subscriptions or project-based watch resources.
Controls polling, batch size, message format, one-time runs, and cleanup.
Can write each watched message to a separate JSON file in a chosen directory.
limitations: Requires the gws CLI and Google Workspace authentication before use.
Gmail watch registrations expire after seven days and must be renewed.
May create Pub/Sub resources unless an existing subscription is supplied.
Email output can contain sensitive personal or business data.

use_cases.description: Watch new customer emails and stream matching messages for triage or routing.

use_cases.title: Feed Email Events to Pipelines
use_cases.description: Capture Gmail watch output for downstream processing in internal data workflows.

use_cases.title: Validate Workspace Notifications

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Watch
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gws-gmail-watch to start a Gmail watch. Explain required authentication checks before running the command.

prompt_templates.title: Watch One Label Once
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gws-gmail-watch to pull unread INBOX messages once. Use metadata format and summarize what each message represents.

prompt_templates.title: Use an Existing Subscription
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gws-gmail-watch with an existing Pub/Sub subscription. Keep resources in place and report any setup assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: Archive Watched Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gws-gmail-watch to watch a project, filter INBOX messages, write output files, and clean up created resources on exit.

output_examples.input: Watch the INBOX label once and summarize new messages.
output_examples.output: The skill starts a one-time Gmail watch, pulls matching messages, and summarizes sender, subject, time, and label context.

output_examples.input: Use an existing Pub/Sub subscription for Gmail watch events.
output_examples.output: The skill connects to the named subscription, streams received message events, and leaves existing resources untouched.

output_examples.input: Capture watched Gmail messages to files and clean up afterward.
output_examples.output: The skill stores each message separately, reports the output directory and message count, then removes created watch resources.

best_practices: Use label filters to limit watched messages to the smallest necessary scope.
Prefer metadata format when full message bodies are not required.
Use cleanup when temporary Pub/Sub resources should not persist.
anti_patterns: Do not stream raw email content into shared logs or public channels.
Do not leave temporary Pub/Sub resources running without an owner.
Do not use broad label scopes when a narrow label filter is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill send email?
faq.answer: No. It watches Gmail for new messages and streams message events.

faq.question: Does it require Google Cloud Pub/Sub?
faq.answer: Yes. Gmail watch workflows use Pub/Sub resources or an existing subscription.

faq.question: How long does a Gmail watch last?
faq.answer: Gmail watch registrations expire after seven days, so they must be renewed.

faq.question: Can it watch only specific messages?
faq.answer: It can filter by Gmail label IDs such as INBOX or UNREAD.

faq.question: Can it save messages to files?
faq.answer: Yes. The output directory option writes each watched message as a separate JSON file.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
